title: Legume rotation effects on subsequent crop yield
research_question: Does including a legume in crop rotation increase the yield of the subsequent non-legume crop?

population.description: Field crops grown after a legume pre-crop in rotation experiments

intervention.description: Legume-based crop rotation (legume grown as the preceding crop before the target crop)

comparator.description: Continuous cropping or non-legume rotation (cereal after cereal, fallow, or non-legume break crop)
comparator.definition: No legume in preceding crop or continuous monoculture

primary.description: Subsequent crop grain yield per unit area
primary.direction_of_interest: positive (legume rotation expected to increase yield)

intervention: Legume-based crop rotation (legume as preceding crop)
primary_outcomes: Subsequent crop grain yield (kg/ha, Mg/ha, t/ha)
typical_effect_size: +20% yield increase (range +10% to +30% depending on crop and region)
important_moderators: Legume species (soybean, pea, lentil, chickpea, faba bean, clover, lupin)
Subsequent crop species (wheat, maize, barley, sorghum, rice)
N fertilizer rate applied to subsequent crop (kg/ha)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield of the SUBSEQUENT CROP (after legume), NOT the legume yield itself
2. Treatment = crop grown AFTER a legume; Control = crop grown after non-legume or in monoculture
5. Record which legume species was the preceding crop
6. Record the subsequent crop species and N fertilizer rate
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is the SUBSEQUENT CROP yield after legume rotation, NOT the legume yield
Control is the same crop grown after a non-legume or in continuous monoculture
Some papers report legume yield AND subsequent crop yield - extract ONLY the subsequent crop
N fertilizer levels may differ between treatments - record exact rates
Multi-year rotation studies: extract each rotation cycle separately
Some papers compare multiple legume species - extract each vs same control

search.seed_papers_description: Zhao et al. 2022 (PNAS, global legume rotation meta-analysis), Peoples et al. 2009, Angus et al. 2015

inclusion_criteria: Primary field experiment comparing legume vs non-legume rotation
Reports yield data for the subsequent (non-legume) crop
Includes a legume pre-crop treatment and a non-legume or monoculture control
exclusion_criteria: Only reports legume yield, not subsequent crop yield

published_pooled_effect.notes: Overall +20% yield increase; wheat +20%, maize +22%, barley +16%; larger with no N fertilizer (+28%) vs high N (+10%)
